(3) On each bare cut end, pull out the cross threads for 1.25" with a toothpick so it gets the same fringe as the factory end. Run a thin bead of fabric glue across the scarf just above each new fringe and along both long cut edges; dry 24 h. (4) Tie once round the neck at the side with both fringed ends hanging in front, over the wire.

Part the curly pile, put a dot of hot glue under the pad and each toe and press 30 s, then run a thin bead of fabric glue round the edges; dry flat.

bones.name: Bone ornaments (makes 8): 9" puffy biscuit bones of air-dry foam clay over a foil core, painted biscuit, sealed, hung level from two gold cords
bones.notes: The board's bones are about as long as the dog is tall (7-11"), chunky like a biscuit (shaft about 0.27 of the length, knob span about 0.53), and hang level from two gold cords. Each takes about 117 g of wet foam clay over a foil core and weighs about 100 g dry.
bones.how: Per bone (template page 4: 9" long, knob span 4.8", shaft 2.4", about 1" thick). Start the day the clay lands: only the painting waits for the DeSerres parcel. (1) Core: scrunch a 12 x 18" sheet of foil into a flat bone about 1/2" thick and 1/4" inside the page-4 outline all round, with a firm ball in each of the four knobs. Wire anchors: twist a small loop at one end of a 4" piece of floral wire and wrap its tail tightly round the foil inside each of the two upper knobs, with the loop just under the surface at the red marks. (2) Clay: on a piece of the drop sheet, lay two pencils 5" apart as 1/4" thickness guides (or two of the 6 mm wood sticks once DeSerres arrives) and press about 120 g of foam clay between them into a 1/4" sheet with a flat flap cut from the XL moving box. Wrap the core, smooth the seams with a damp finger and shape four round knobs and a flat-faced shaft against the page-4 outline. Dry 48 h, turning once. (3) Paint: 2 coats of the biscuit mix (1/2 cup gesso + 2 tsp deep ochre + 1 tsp burnt sienna); dry-brush burnt sienna on the edges and knobs; 1 coat of Mod Podge. (4) Hang with two cords, level, like the board: drill a hole about 3/4" deep at each red mark by twisting a toothpick down to the wire anchor. Cut a 50 cm gold cord, knot each end twice, fill each hole with hot glue and push one knotted end into each, so the glue grips the anchor. The two cords rise from the upper knobs and the bone hangs level; hang it from the middle of the cord and wire the cord to the branch with 8" of floral wire.

bones_small.how: As the 9" bones, against the 5" outline on page 9: foil cores about 1/4" thick, about 3/4" thick finished (about 36 g of clay each), the same two wire anchors at the red marks, then paint, seal, and the gold cord glued into two drilled holes.

cascades.name: Tartan ribbon cascades (makes 5): 4" tartan from under the topper to the bottom branches, with poufs
cascades.notes: The board's tartan runs from the topper to the bottom branches in loose poufs, with the big bows sitting on it. Five cascades, evenly round the tree, so the back is decorated too.
cascades.how: (1) Cut five 118" lengths of the 4" tartan (rolls 1 and 2 of the cut plan under the big bows). V-notch one end of each and seal it with a thin bead of fabric glue. (2) Space them evenly round the tree, about 72 degrees apart. Tuck the square end under the topper bow, about 8" below the tip, and wire it to the top stem with 6" of floral wire. (3) Work down and slightly round the tree: let the ribbon lie over the branch tips for about 12", then pinch it up into a pouf about 3" proud (about 8" of ribbon) and wire the pinch to a branch with 6" of floral wire. Make 4 poufs per cascade, about 10 ties in all, and finish at the bottom branches about 12" off the floor with the notched tail hanging free. (4) Wire 2-3 of the big tartan bows onto each cascade at a pouf, as on the board.

cat_fluffy.name: Grey-and-white cat plush, standing, 8" long x 7" tall (FLUFFYFUN)
cat_fluffy.notes: Mostly white with grey patches; stripes only on the head; stands on four legs with its tail up (gallery size chart: 7" tall x 8" long). The board's cats are striped tabbies sitting upright. Third-party seller Fluffyfun with 4 ratings, $5.45 delivery Nov 24.

cat_miyoni.name: Grey tabby kitten plush, 9" long x 6" tall, crouching (Aurora Miyoni Tots)

It crouches (front paws forward, head up) where the board's cats sit upright, so it lies along a branch on the tree. Snip off the gold Miyoni tag; the scarf covers the spot. Sold by Amazon US (cross-border, no import fee shown), 4.8 stars from 2,170 ratings, free delivery Nov 20, but only 8 left on Nov 16: order it first.
cat_miyoni.how: Each cat (about 136 g): snip off the gold Miyoni tag. Fold a 48" floral wire in half, wrap the doubled wire round the body behind the front legs, under the scarf, and twist both ends round a sturdy branch so the cat lies along it, face out. Under the tree it sits beside the dog (see the golden retriever).

crown.name: Gold crown (makes 1): 12 gold glitter sprays fanned behind the topper bow
crown.notes: Not on the board: an extra. Uses a second pack of gold sprays (the first pack goes through the tree).
crown.how: (1) Before the topper goes on, fan 12 gold sprays in a half-circle behind where the bow will sit, stems pushed into the top branches. (2) Wire each stem to the top stem with 6" of floral wire. (3) Fix the bow in front, then bend the sprays so they show evenly round the loops.

ct_supplies.notes: Pick up at Canadian Tire Edmonton South (2110 101 St NW) with the moving boxes. Scotch Magic Tape is $4.99 on sale until Nov 18 ($7.49 after); the plan counts $7.49.

doghouse.name: Doghouse ornaments (makes 6): 10" foam-board doghouses, dark-jointed red brick walls, cream plank roof with barge boards and ridge cap, arched door with flat cream trim and threshold, raised cream paw on the gable
doghouse.notes: Built at the board's scale: its doghouse is about as tall as the dog beside it (10-15"). Each weighs about 160 g (about 350 sq in of 3/16" foam board, 50 g of paint, 4 glue sticks), so it sits upright on a sturdy inner branch, wired through the floor, like the board's, with the gold loop as a safety tie.
doghouse.how: Print pages 1, 2 and 8 at Actual size (check the 1" square). Cut on the flattened moving box with a fresh blade against the steel ruler; mark in pencil, never pen. Test the glue gun on an offcut first and glue onto the paper faces, not the bare foam edge (the hot gun melts the foam core). (1) Cut, per house, following the page-2 cut plan (boards 1-9 hold all six houses; board 10 is spare; measure each board first and if it is under 16" trim the difference off the roof overhang): front with the arched door (keep the door piece), back, two sides, two roofs, floor (page 2), four corner trims (page 2), and from page 8 the flat U-shaped arch trim (cut as one piece), two barge boards (flip one), the threshold and two ridge caps. Cut the 2.5" gable paw (pad + 4 toes, page 8) from the door piece. (2) Score while the template is still taped on: press the grey brick lines (page 1: courses about 0.9", bricks 1.5", staggered) and the roof board lines (page 2: every 1.25" parallel to the eave, joints every 1.5") through the paper with the empty ballpoint. Score the two plank lines on the threshold. (3) Paint flat, before assembly: the inside faces of the walls and the undersides of both roofs burnt sienna (stops the foam board warping; dark through the door); the roof tops, trims, threshold and paw one coat of cream (cream = 1/2 cup (120 ml) gesso + 1 tsp deep ochre + a pea-sized dab of burnt sienna; mix one batch for all six houses in a lidded cup and stir with a wood stick). (4) Assemble with hot glue: the walls round the floor (the floor sits inside the walls), then a toothpick across the inside of the two gable peaks with a 60 cm gold cord tied round it, the doubled loop coming out at the ridge, then the two roofs (3/4" overhang all round) either side of the cord. Poke two holes through the floor 2" apart with a toothpick. (5) Walls: brush the outside dark brick (dark brick = Crimson + Lamp Black about 10:1) and let it dry, then sponge-dab barn red = Naphthol Red + Crimson 1:1 over the brick faces only, twice, so the scored joints stay dark like the board's. (6) Second cream coat on the roof, trims, threshold and paw; dry-brush a little sienna along the roof boards for grain. Paint the ridge caps barn red with a touch of sienna. (7) Trims: glue the four corner trims on the wall corners, the threshold flat at the foot of the door (back edge against the wall, top level with the floor, sticking out 3/4"), the U arch trim round the door with its legs standing on the threshold, the barge boards along the two front roof edges meeting at the peak, the ridge caps as a peak over the ridge either side of the cord, and the five paw pieces on the front gable centred 2.84" below the peak (dotted on page 1). Darken the inside of the door opening with a little Lamp Black. (8) Hang: push a 10" floral wire through each floor hole, sit the house upright on a sturdy inner branch near the trunk and twist the wires round the branch; tie the gold loop to the branch above as a safety tie. About 40 min each once cut.
tools: Pencil and an empty ballpoint pen (office)

doghouse_small.name: Doghouse ornaments (makes 12): 4.3" foam-board doghouses
doghouse_small.notes: Same build at the earlier size: a third of the board's doghouse, so it reads as filler rather than a feature. About 30 g each.
doghouse_small.how: Template page 5 (Letter): front and back (door 1.5 x 1.9"), two sides, two roofs, floor, four corner trims, the flat U arch trim, two barge boards, two ridge caps and the threshold. Cut 12 sets on the flattened box and score the 0.4" brick courses printed on page 5 with the empty ballpoint. Then as the 10" house: sienna inside and under the roofs and a first cream coat while flat; glue up with a toothpick bar and a 30 cm gold loop at the peak; dark brick base, then dabbed barn red; second cream coat; trims. For the gable paw, cut a stencil of the 1" paw (page 3) from the drafting film and dab cream through it with the sponge. Hang from the gold loop and wire it to the branch with 8" of floral wire.
tools: Pencil and an empty ballpoint pen (office)

doghouse_xl.name: Giant doghouse (makes 1): 24 x 20 x 26" from two moving boxes, red brick walls, cream shingle roof, "Home for the Howlidays" sign
doghouse_xl.notes: Not on the board: an extra we can add for impact. The plush pair sits in the doorway.
doghouse_xl.how: (1) Box A: cut all four walls down to 16" with the art knife against the ruler, keeping the bottom flaps taped as the floor. Cut the 10 x 13" arched door in a 24" side (true-size door on template page 6, cut plan on page 7). (2) Box B: cut two 24 x 10" gable triangles from its long flaps and glue them on top of the front and back walls; cut two 17.6 x 24" roof panels from its 24 x 20" sides. Packing-tape every inside seam. (3) Score brick lines on all walls with the empty ballpoint (courses about 2", bricks 4"). Gesso the outside twice, tinted grey with a drop of black, dab red bricks with the sponge, and paint the inside dark red-brown. (4) Glue the roof on, then cover it with 3" strips cut from box B's spare sides and the gable offcuts, overlapping 1" per course, and paint them cream (cream = 1/2 cup (120 ml) gesso + 1 tsp deep ochre + a pea-sized dab of burnt sienna). (5) Glue a cream trim strip round the door and stencil a 3.6" cream paw on the gable (a drafting-film stencil cut from page 3). (6) Mod Podge the printed 16 x 4" sign (HP26_Doghouse_Sign_11x17.pdf) centred on the front with its top edge 18.5" above the floor, so its corners clear the roof. About 4 hours over two sessions.

faux_treats.name: Faux dog biscuits (makes 64): foam clay cut with the 2.7" bone cutter, painted tan, sealed; set ring by ring against the glass of the jar
faux_treats.notes: The board's biscuits are small and tan in a 7" jar, so we cut them with the smallest bone cutter (2.7"), not the 3". 7 per ring x 7 rings line the glass, plus 12 on top: 61; we make 64. Inedible, so they last until the 2027 auction.
faux_treats.how: (1) Biscuits: on a piece of the drop sheet, press foam clay into a 1/4" sheet between two 6 mm wood sticks with a foam-board offcut, cut 64 bones with the 2.7" cutter (no cutter yet? trace the 3" outline on page 4 and cut with the knife), poke 3 dots in each with a toothpick and dry 24 h flat, turning once. Paint 2 coats of the tan mix (1/4 cup gesso + 2 tsp deep ochre + 1 tsp burnt sienna), then 1 coat of Mod Podge. (2) Jar, ring by ring: stand 7 biscuits flat against the glass (long side level, face out), stuff crumpled kraft paw paper (3 spare sheets, brown side out) behind them until they press on the glass, and repeat for 7 rings up to the shoulder; pile the last 12 on top. Nudge them into place through the mouth with a wood stick. (3) Wrap a 22" velvet band round the shoulder and hot-glue it at the back, tie a bow over the seam (44": two 5" loops, 9" tails), and fix the lid with 3 dots of hot glue (peels off later).
tools: A foam-board offcut (on the list) to press the clay

felt.name: Black felt sheets, 8" x 12" (paw on the bone pillow)
felt.notes: 1 mm black felt; cut a 4" paw and glue it to the sherpa pillow.
felt.how: One pack of 8 x 12" black felt covers every felt paw: 24 x 3" for the topper, 1 x 3" for the basket bone toy, 12 x 1" for the stocking cuffs and 1 x 4.5" for the bone pillow (all on template page 3). Trace with the white fabric marker; the hoop-ornament back circles use the DeSerres 9 x 12" sheets.

floral_wire.name: Green floral wire, 22-gauge (3 rolls), required to secure every ornament
floral_wire.notes: Green 22-gauge paddle wire, 3 spools of 118 yd. Sold by Amazon US (cross-border), 4.8 stars from 1,208, $29.19, free delivery Nov 19 (re-checked Nov 16).

gift_boxes.name: Wrapped gifts (makes 4): moving boxes in tartan and kraft paw paper, cream burlap ribbon and bows, a tartan band and bow on the kraft box
gift_boxes.notes: Like the board: tartan boxes tied with cream ribbon and cream bows, and a kraft paw-print box with a tartan band and bow and a cream band with its own bow. Four bought boxes of known size, so paper and ribbon are calculated.
gift_boxes.how: Boxes: A = small (18 x 11 x 12") as is, B = medium (16") as is, C = medium cut to 10" tall, D = small cut to 7" tall. (1) Fold and packing-tape the top flaps of all four shut. For C and D, mark the new height up from the open bottom on each corner, rule a pencil line round the box and cut the walls down along it with the art knife against the ruler, on the cutting box. The open bottom sits on the floor, hidden. (2) Tartan paper on A, B and C: cut two lengths of the box's girth (A 48", B 66", C 54") from the 17" roll and Magic-Tape them edge to edge on the back (1/2" overlap). Wrap so this join runs round the middle of the box, where the cream ribbon will cover it, with the girth overlap underneath; fold the ends like a parcel and tape (B's ends overlap only about 3/4": tape them well). (3) Kraft paw paper on D: two 17 x 40" sheets taped side by side, wrapped the same way with the join under the tartan band. (4) Ribbon: 1.5" cream burlap both ways round A, B and C, crossing on top over the paper join, ends taped underneath. On D, a 40" tartan band round the girth over the join and a 62" cream burlap band round the four sides, ends taped at the back. (5) Bows: tie a 10" cream burlap bow (40": two 5" loops, 6" tails, V-notched, pinched with 6" of floral wire) for each box and hot-glue it at the ribbon crossing (on D, on the front of the cream band). Tie one big tartan bow (as the tree bows) and hot-glue it on top of D at the tartan band.

holiday_toy.notes: The board's basket toy is a curly cream sherpa bone with a big black paw. Ethical Pet's cream fleece bone has that texture and colour; glue a 3" black felt paw on its face. The earlier link (B0GR99NF8V) was the Gray variant, and its sibling B0GR99XYFS is listed as White. Sold by Amazon.ca, 3.8 stars from 1,437, free delivery Nov 20.
holiday_toy.how: Trace one 3" paw (template page 3) on the black felt with the white fabric marker and cut it out (pad + 4 toes). Part the sherpa pile, put a dot of hot glue under the pad and each toe and press 30 s, then run a thin bead of fabric glue round the edges; dry flat. Wire it into the basket with 12" of floral wire.

mini_bows.name: Mini red velvet bows, 3.5" (12-pk)
mini_bows.notes: Small deep-red velvet bows on twist ties.

paw_disc.name: Paw ornaments (makes 10): 6" hoops painted gold, tea-stained Aida face, black glitter paw, felt back, dark red velvet bow
paw_disc.notes: The board's paw ornament is a warm biscuit-cream textured disc in a gold rim with a gold cap, a black sparkly paw and a deep red velvet bow. A 6" embroidery hoop gives the gold rim, and its brass screw sits where the cap is; tea-stained Aida gives the woven texture and the warm colour.
paw_disc.how: Per ornament (template pages 3 and 9). (1) Hoop: paint the outer ring only. Prime its outside face and front edge with gesso, then 2 coats of gold; leave the inner ring, the outer ring's inside face and the brass screw bare (paint there makes the clamp too tight and scuffs off). Paint one spare hoop with them. Cure 24 h. (2) Face: cut the Aida into 9 x 9" pieces (4 per sheet, 2 spare). Tea-stain them: 4 black tea bags in 1 L of just-boiled water for 10 min, soak the pieces 10 min, rinse once and dry flat under a towel (no tea: 1/4 tsp deep ochre and a drop of burnt sienna in 1 cup of water). Stain an offcut strip first and let it dry to check: it should be the board's warm biscuit-cream, not white. (3) Hoop it: lay a piece over the inner ring, press the outer ring down with the screw at the top, pull the edges evenly all round until drum-tight and tighten the screw. On the back trim the Aida to 1/2" outside the ring and hot-glue that margin to the inside of the inner ring. (4) Paw: cut a 3.6" paw (pad + 4 toes, page 3) from the black glitter cardstock and glue it to the centre with fabric glue. (5) Back: trace a 6" circle (page 9) on black felt with the white fabric marker, cut it out and hot-glue it to the back edge of the inner ring over the trimmed Aida, so the ornament is finished from behind. (6) Bow and hanger: tie a 9" bow from 37" of the velvet (two 4.5" loops, 8" tails, V-notched), wire it just above the screw with 8" of floral wire, and tie a 25 cm gold cord loop through the screw to hang it; twist the wire ends round the branch.
tools: Black tea bags, a kettle and a bowl (office kitchen)

paw_disc_fay.name: Paw ornaments (makes 10): Faylapa 6" bamboo hoops (16-pk) painted gold, tea-stained Aida face, black glitter paw, felt back, velvet bow

paw_disc_wood.name: Paw ornaments (makes 30): 4" bauble-shaped wood rounds painted cream, gold rim and cap, black sparkle paw, mini velvet bow
paw_disc_wood.notes: The earlier design: more of them, but two-thirds of the board's size and a flat painted face.
paw_disc_wood.how: (1) Paint both sides cream (cream = 1/2 cup (120 ml) gesso + 1 tsp deep ochre + a pea-sized dab of burnt sienna) twice, the rim and cap gold. (2) Cut a stencil of the 3" paw (page 3) from the drafting film with the art knife and sponge-dab black through it; add the black sparkle medium. (3) Seal with Mod Podge. (4) Tie a 25 cm gold cord loop through the hole, hot-glue a mini bow at the cap and wire it to a branch with 6" of floral wire.

red4_joyin.name: Red baubles, 4": glossy, matte, glitter and mirror (JOYIN 4-pc)

streamers.name: Topper streamers (makes 2): 90" of the topper ribbon draped down the front with poufs and felt paws
streamers.notes: Not on the board: an extra. Cut from the same roll as the topper, so they always match the chosen bow.
streamers.how: (1) Cut two 90" lengths of the topper ribbon (5 yd with the gathers). V-notch one end of each and seal both cut ends with a thin bead of fabric glue. (2) Trace 24 paws with the 3" template (page 3) on the black felt with the white fabric marker and glue 12 on the front face of each streamer, about every 7"; dry flat. (3) Tuck the square end of each under the topper knot and wire it to the top stem with 6" of floral wire. (4) Drape them down the front in loose S-curves: pinch a pouf about every 14" and wire each pinch to a branch tip with 6" of floral wire (6 ties each).

tabby_brown.notes: Douglas Zigby: striped grey-brown tabby with a white bib, standing. Sold by Toy-Mart & Plus, shipped by Amazon from outside Canada ("Extended delivery time: Shipped internationally"), 4.5 stars from 390 ratings, $5.21 delivery Nov 19.

tabby_grey.notes: Sitting grey tabby with a white chest: the board's pose and coat, but a third to a half of its size. Sold by Amazon.ca, 4.3 stars from 42 ratings.

tartan_ribbon.name: Red/green/black tartan wired ribbon, 4" x 10 yd
tartan_ribbon.notes: 4" wired tartan: the board's red-and-green plaid with a thin gold line. Cascades, hand-tied bows and the paw-paper gift's ribbon. Sold by GiftWrap Etc. and shipped by Amazon from outside Canada (4.7 stars, 146): $5.45 delivery, Nov 24. Order it first. The plan counts the $5.45 once per roll (worst case); confirm the delivery line at checkout. Fallback: MESEEY B0FFH6C6HL (brighter red and green with a gold edge, $27.71 + $5.35, Nov 24, also international).

tartan_wrap.name: Red tartan wrapping paper (reversible)
tartan_wrap.notes: Old roll was green with tan check. New: red tartan with green & white lines, like the boxes in the photo.

topper.name: Tree topper (makes 1): 22" burlap bow, two upswept loops and two 14" tails, 6" natural jute with 3" black felt paws, wired edges
topper.notes: The board's bow: natural burlap about 6" wide, two big upswept loops over shorter tails, black paws about half the ribbon's width. No paw-print burlap is sold at this width, so we glue on 3" felt paws; floral wire glued along the back edges lets the unwired jute hold its shape like the board. Vendor: the 6" jute (B0DQ4BXYKZ) is sold by xingwanworks (18 ratings) and shipped by Amazon from outside Canada, $6.43, Nov 22; the 4" wired burlap (B0CHMLF3NP, Nov 20) is the fallback. The jute is not wired, so the glued edge wire is essential.
topper.how: Cut list from the 6" jute (12 yd roll): one 78" bow strip and one 8" knot piece (2.4 yd with the notches). Work on the drop sheet. (1) Edge wire: on the back face, hot-glue a 79" length of floral wire 1/4" in from each long edge, folding the last 1/2" of wire back at each end so it cannot poke out. The jute is not wired, so this is what holds the loops. (2) Paws, front face only: trace 24 paws on the black felt with the 3" template (page 3) and the white fabric marker (or tape the paper paw to the felt and cut round it). Each paw is 5 pieces: a pad and four toes. Glue 23 on the front face of the strip with fabric glue, alternating left and right of the centre line about every 3.4", none in the middle 4" where the bow is pinched; glue the 24th in the middle of the knot piece. Dry flat overnight. (3) Fray stop: the long edges are hemmed; run a thin bead of fabric glue across the cut ends of the strip and the knot piece. (4) Tie, paws facing you: leave a 14" tail, make a 10" loop to the left (about 22" of ribbon) and a 10" loop to the right, angling both loops up about 20 degrees, and pinch the centre with an 18" piece of floral wire; the second 14" tail hangs down. Fold the knot piece lengthwise in half (3" wide, paw out), wrap it round the pinch and hot-glue it at the back. V-notch both tails 1" deep and seal the notch with fabric glue. (5) Fix: zip-tie it to the top stem with two of the organizers' zip ties and twist the 18" wire ends round the stem (two more 18" wires if it leans). Shape the loops up and round and let the tails hang about 25 degrees off vertical, like the board: about 22" across with 14" tails.
tools: Zip ties (2, supplied with the tree)

topper_4in.name: Tree topper (makes 1): 24" four-loop bow from 4" wired burlap with black felt paws
topper_4in.notes: The earlier design: four loops of 4" ribbon. Thinner and busier than the board's two fat loops.
topper_4in.how: (1) Cut 2.6 yd of the 4" wired burlap: one 86" bow strip and one 8" knot piece (it is wired, so no edge wire). (2) Trace 16 black felt paws with the 3" template (page 3) and the white fabric marker; glue them on the front face with fabric glue, alternating sides about every 5"; dry flat. (3) Make four 6" loops (two up, two down), pinch with an 18" floral wire, wrap the knot piece round the centre and hot-glue it at the back, leave two 16" tails, V-notch them and seal the cut ends with fabric glue. (4) Zip-tie it to the top with the organizers' zip ties and the wire ends.
tools: Zip ties (2, supplied with the tree)

topper_printed.name: Tree topper (makes 1): 20" bow from ready-printed 2.5" burlap paw ribbon (brown paws)
topper_printed.notes: No cutting or gluing of paws, but the paws are brown and the ribbon is less than half the board's width.
topper_printed.how: (1) Cut 2.4 yd of the printed 2.5" ribbon (it is wired): one 80" strip and one 6" knot piece. (2) Make a four-loop bow 20" across (loops about 5"), pinch with an 18" floral wire, wrap the knot piece round it and hot-glue it at the back. (3) Leave two 14" tails, V-notch them and seal the cut ends with fabric glue. (4) Zip-tie to the top with the organizers' zip ties and the wire ends.
tools: Zip ties (2, supplied with the tree)

velvet_ribbon.name: Dark red wired velvet ribbon, 1.5" x 25 yd (bows on the paw ornaments, the tree and the jar)
velvet_ribbon.form_name: Dark red velvet ribbon, 1.5" x 25 yd
velvet_ribbon.notes: The board mixes solid deep red velvet bows with the tartan on the tree, and its paw-ornament and jar bows are the same velvet with soft loops and long tails. MEEDEE "dark red" is that colour; hand-tied, a 9" bow uses about 1 yd. Ships from and sold by Amazon US (cross-border; 4.6 stars from 1,350): check the checkout for an import-fee line.

velvet_tree_bows.name: Velvet bows for the tree, 9" with 8" tails (hand-tied from the 1.5" dark red velvet)
velvet_tree_bows.notes: The board mixes solid deep red velvet bows with the tartan ones on the tree. Tied from the velvet roll we already buy, so they cost nothing extra.
velvet_tree_bows.how: Each bow: 37" of the 1.5" velvet: two 4.5" loops and 8" tails with V-notches, pinched with a 12" floral wire (as the paw-ornament bows). Wire them between the tartan bows, mostly on the right side and lower half like the board.
